4426515.story: Nacua is also dealing with a PCL sprain and turf toe, but the only procedure he required was for his MCL. With a firmer 4-to-5-month timeline now in place for the star wideout, he'll be done for the season while the Rams look to others to help fill the massive void in their receiver corps. Davante Adams (hamstring) should eventually take on a heavy target share, but he's also on injured reserve and isn't expected to return until at least Week 13. 4426515.headline: Coach Sean McVay revealed Friday that Nacua (knee) had surgery to repair his MCL on Tuesday and is on track to miss a couple of months, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
4426515.story: Given that timetable, Nacua -- who already is on injured reserve -- could be out for the rest of the regular season, which is a huge blow to the Rams' pass-catching corps going forward. In Nacua's continued absence, Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith are the team's healthy options at WR, though fellow starter Davante Adams (hamstring) is believed to be targeting a return in Week 12 following the team's bye.

4426515.headline: Nacua has been suspended three games for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
4426515.story: Nacua currently resides on injured reserve due to PCL and MCL sprains and a turf toe injury, for which he still must miss at least three games. The announced suspension conveniently lines up with his remaining expected time away from the field, and he'll be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, Dec. 14, following the completion of the the Rams' Week 14 contest versus the 49ers. 3929630.headline: Barkley suffered a stinger during Thursday's game in Dallas.
3929630.story: This marks Barkley's second diagnosed stinger of the campaign, but on the previous occasion in Week 2 against the Titans, he was able to check back in to the contest. The Eagles may opt to exercise caution with Barkley, however, because he tended to a neck issue on a short week following this past Sunday's win against the Steelers.

3929630.headline: The Eagles listed Barkley (neck/illness) as a full participant in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
3929630.story: Though Tuesday's injury report was merely an estimate, Barkley would have been able to take every rep had the Eagles held a traditional practice session. Barkley emerged from this past Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers with a neck injury and an illness, but neither health concern looks like it will prevent him from playing Thursday in Dallas.

3929630.headline: Barkley was listed as a limited participant on Monday's estimated practice report due to a neck injury and an illness.
3929630.story: Barkley appeared to be nursing a left arm injury in the aftermath of Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers, but it was instead two different health concerns that resulted in him being included on the Eagles' first Week 12 injury report. The Eagles are facing a quick turnaround this week with a Thursday matchup against the Cowboys, so Barkley could be in line for only light activity over the next two days as the team aims to keep him as fresh as possible for that contest. Head coach Nick Sirianni hasn't yet offered any indication that Barkley is in jeopardy of sitting out Thanksgiving Day.

4426338.headline: Nix completed 22 of 40 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions in Friday's 27-5 loss to the Steelers. He also rushed once for seven yards and lost a fumble.
4426338.story: Nix was directly responsible for two first-half Pittsburgh touchdowns, as T.J. Watt recovered a Nix fumble in the end zone to open the scoring and Jalen Ramsey scored on a pick-six to extend Pittsburgh's lead to 24-5. Neither offense did much after halftime as Nix continued to struggle. Friday's dud drops Nix's season average to just 193 passing yards per game to go with a 12:7 TD:INT through 11 starts, but the Broncos still boast an excellent 8-3 record heading into a Week 13 home game against the Dolphins.

4426338.headline: Nix completed 19 of 35 passes for 225 yards, one touchdown and one interception and notched six carries for five yards during Sunday's 38-24 victory against the Raiders.
4426338.story: After a hit-or-miss first six appearances of the season, Nix has settled into a four-game stretch in which his passing yards have ranged from 222 to 237 weekly, a span in which he boasts a 6:2 TD:INT and 84 rushing yards and another score. He also displayed some promise with offseason acquisition Jaylen Waddle (3-61-0 on six targets) while connecting with TE Adam Trautman for his 12th touchdown pass in 10 contests. Nix will look to keep things rolling Friday at Pittsburgh.

4258173.headline: Collins secured three of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
4258173.story: Facing a Colts defense down both Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee), Collins looked primed for a big night early when he recorded a 42-yard touchdown grab to cap off Houston's second possession. However, C.J. Stroud proceeded to spread the ball around to nine different targets overall, leading to Collins tying his second-lowest reception tally and posting his third-lowest yardage total of the season. However, the star wideout did extend his touchdown streak to three games, and he'll next take aim at what has been an inconsistent Ravens secondary in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday

4258173.headline: Collins secured nine of 16 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
4258173.story: Collins comfortably paced the Texans across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and he added his fifth touchdown of the season on a 12-yard catch in the first quarter. Collins also had a 16-yard reception on Houston's last-gasp drive wiped out by an offensive holding penalty, but he still finished with season highs in receptions and targets. Collins retains an unquestioned No. 1 role in the Texans' prolific air attack, affording him an enticing combination of floor and upside heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

4431611.headline: Williams said after Thursday's 39-35 win in Detroit that he's "fine" and likely just has "a bruise on his abdomen," Jason Lieser of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.
4431611.story: Williams seemingly went for a precautionary X-ray after Week 12 action due to a "weird fall" that occurred during Thursday's contest in which he engineered two TD drives in the final 8:20 of the fourth quarter to eke out a four-point victory. He completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and recorded three carries for 15 yards. With plenty of time to recover before the Bears' next game Sunday, Dec. 6 against the Jaguars, Williams has a decent chance to avoid practice restrictions next week.

4431611.headline: Williams is having an X-ray performed after Thursday's 39-35 win at Detroit, Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune reports.
4431611.story: The Bears found themselves down 35-24 with 8:20 remaining in the fourth quarter, but some heroics by Williams resulted in two touchdowns for the visitors down the stretch, including a six-yard dot to WR Rome Odunze with three seconds left. Overall, Williams attempted a season-high 44 passes, completing 30 of them for 345 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. He also had three carries for 15 yards. In the aftermath of the contest, Williams appears to have sustained an injury, but its nature isn't known just yet.

4431611.headline: Williams completed 15 of 23 passes for 181 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints. He added 11 rushing yards on four carries.
4431611.story: The Bears' offense looked a little sluggish coming out of its bye, and both of Williams' TD passes came in the second quarter as he connected with D'Andre Swift on a three-yard shovel pass and Colston Loveland on a 15-yard score. Williams failed to reach 200 passing yards for the first time since Week 2, and he'll take a somewhat disappointing 10:6 TD:INT through seven games into a Week 12 clash with the Lions.

4431611.headline: Williams completed 22 of 37 passes for 279 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. He also rushed five times for 16 yards.
4431611.story: Williams looked unstoppable early, capping Chicago's two first-quarter drives with touchdown passes of nine yards to Rome Odunze and 56 yards to Luther Burden, the latter of whom later exited due to a concussion. The 2024 first overall pick cooled down after that, throwing three second-quarter interceptions en route to a career-worst four interceptions overall. Chicago's defense picked up the slack with a pick-six against Baker Mayfield, and Williams found Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning field goal on the game's final play. 4432620.headline: Washington (shoulder) will be out for Sunday's game against the Titans and is considered week-to-week moving forward, Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports.
4432620.story: Washington was added to Jacksonville's injury report Thursday due to a shoulder injury, and the impact of the injury has escalated from limiting his practice participation Thursday to sidelining Jacksonville's top receiver Sunday and possibly beyond then. In Washington's absence, Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and possibly Travis Hunter or CJ Williams -- to a lesser degree -- could garner more attention from Trevor Lawrence against a Titans secondary that has allowed the most catches and yards per game in the league to wide receivers. Additional details regarding Washington'

4432620.headline: Washington (shoulder) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
4432620.story: Washington wasn't on Wednesday's injury report, so his addition to it a day later is certainly of note. It remains to be seen if the WR, who is coming off consecutive big games for the Jaguars, is managing a shoulder issue stemming from Week 11 action or was hurt in Thursday's practice. Friday's report will reveal both Washington's participation level to close the week, as well as his game status for a 1:00 p.m. ET matchup versus the Titans on Sunday.

4432620.headline: Washington secured eight of 17 targets for 103 yards in the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
4432620.story: Washington led the Jaguars across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his day could have been even better had what appeared to be an acrobatic touchdown catch in the back of the end zone early in the fourth quarter not been ruled incomplete. Washington still made several tough grabs throughout the afternoon against a stingy Giants secondary, and he now has consecutive 100-yard efforts for the first time in 2026. Washington needs just 100 receiving yards to eclipse his career high of 847 heading into a very favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

4038815.headline: Dowdle carried the ball 11 times for 71 yards in Friday's 27-5 win over the Broncos.
4038815.story: Jaylen Warren led the Steelers backfield with 21 touches, but he turned that volume into just 46 yards while Dowdle led the team in rushing. The 71 rushing yards also were a season high for Dowdle, and if Pittsburgh continues to deploy a ground-heavy game plan with Mason Rudolph under center in place of the exiled Aaron Rodgers, there could be plenty of work for both RBs. Dowdle will try to keep making a case for more of a timeshare with Warren in Week 13 against the Texans.

4038815.headline: Dowdle rushed five times for 15 yards and caught four of five targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
4038815.story: Dowdle finished with 34 scrimmage yards for a second consecutive game after racking up 235 scrimmage yards over his preceding four appearances. He had five more yards than Jaylen Warren on two fewer touches in Sunday's loss. Dowdle is poised to retain his spot as the 1B option alongside Warren in Friday's Week 12 home game against the Broncos.

4038815.headline: Dowdle rushed five times for 26 yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Sunday's 38-18 defeat at Cincinnati.
4038815.story: Dowdle's previous low-water mark in touches was nine in Week 2 at New England, and on the season he averaged 11.8 touches per game entering Week 10 action. As a result, he finished with his second-fewest yards from scrimmage (34) in a contest this season, while backfield mate Jaylen Warren (12 touches for 41 total yards) also found little success in any facet. Dowdle remains the No. 2 RB in Pittsburgh behind Warren and thus is a hit-or-miss option in a Week 11 road matchup with the Eagles next Sunday.

4038815.headline: Dowdle rushed 15 times for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
4038815.story: Dowdle finished just two carries behind Jaylen Warren on the afternoon, and although his backfield mate significantly outpaced him in yardage, the former made his fantasy mark when he opened the scoring on the day with a nine-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Dowdle recorded new season highs in rush attempts and rushing yards as the Steelers had the luxury of leaning heavily on the ground attack, but Warren remains the backfield's clear No. 1 option heading into the Week 9 bye.

3040151.headline: Kittle caught all three of his targets for 34 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
3040151.story: Kittle scored on both of his first-half catches, capping San Francisco's opening drive with a 17-yard touchdown before adding an eight-yard score in the first minute of the second quarter. The multi-touchdown performance was especially impressive considering the Vikings came in having allowed just one touchdown on a league-low 33 catches to tight ends. Kittle has been one of the top performers at his position as usual, with seven touchdown catches in 10 games, though his streak of consecutive outings with at least four catches ended at eight games. 3040151.headline: Kittle brought in six of nine targets for 74 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
3040151.story: Kittle put together a very solid fantasy performance that was easily lost in the shuffle of multiple spectacular efforts by players on either side. However, the veteran tight end did pace the 49ers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards, and he's now recorded at least 70 yards on five occasions this season. Kittle is up to a 44-557-5 line on 62 targets through nine games as a Week 11 home showdown against the Vikings next Sunday night approaches.

3040151.headline: Kittle caught four of seven targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
3040151.story: Kittle had at least three more targets than any teammate Sunday but finished 28 receiving yards shy of Jordan Watkins' team-leading total, while Brock Purdy's two touchdown passes went to Christian McCaffrey and Watkins. Sunday's output marked Kittle's third-lowest yardage total of the season, but the star TE recorded at least four catches for a seventh consecutive game. He'll look to add to his season totals of 38 catches for 483 yards and five touchdowns in Week 10 against the Cowboys.

4241416.headline: Hubbard carried the ball 27 times for 120 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens. He added a two-point conversion.
4241416.story: The 27-year-old running back continues to shine, making two trips to the end zone for a second straight week and piling up at least 120 rushing yards for the third time in 2026. Hubbard is handling a bell-cow workload with no issues, and over six games since the Panthers' bye he's averaging nearly 25 touches a game while amassing 688 scrimmage yards and six rushing touchdowns. Jonathon Brooks (groin) seems close to coming off IR, but but he's unlikely to make much of a dent in Hubbard's role as long as the team's top RB is dominating. 3126486.headline: Samuel logged two carries for 27 yards, gathered in three of four targets for 20 yards and returned two kickoffs for 57 yards during Sunday's 35-10 win against the Vikings in Mexico City.
3126486.story: Samuel didn't come close to replicating the 109 yards from scrimmage and two TDs on six touches that he accrued during a Week 10 shootout in Dallas, but he continued to mix into the offense in all realms, as he's ranged from two to eight touches in each of his seven appearances this season. Overall, he's averaging 11.7 yards per catch and a whopping 13.1 yards per carry to go with five total touchdowns in 2026, making him one big play away from producing weekly.

3126486.headline: Samuel rushed three times for 78 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for 31 yards and another score in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
3126486.story: Samuel made his return from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury, and the versatile veteran was put right to work as the de facto No. 1 receiver with Mike Evans (Achilles) still sidelined. Samuel came just a yard short of tying his single-game career high in rushing yards, and his receiving and rushing touchdowns came from 11 and 70 yards out, respectively. Samuel has five total touchdowns through six games heading into a Week 11 home matchup against a tough Vikings defense next Sunday night.

4569987.headline: Warren carried the ball 20 times for 46 yards and caught one of two targets for zero yards in Friday's 27-5 win over the Broncos.
4569987.story: There wasn't much offense happening in this one -- two of Pittsburgh's three touchdowns came on defense, while the Denver defense chipped in a safety -- but Warren had an especially tough day, as his longest gain went for just six yards, and Rico Dowdle wound up leading the Steelers with 71 rushing yards on just 11 carries. The workload split was still encouraging for Warren, as was the ground-heavy game plan with Mason Rudolph taking over at quarterback for the exiled Aaron Rodgers, but the backfield could be drifting back toward a timeshare. 4569987.headline: Warren rushed nine times for 28 yards and caught two of three targets for one yard in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
4569987.story: Warren finished with 29 yards on 11 touches compared to 34 yards on nine touches for Rico Dowdle, as Pittsburgh's backfield duo was held quiet for a second consecutive game. After recording at least 73 scrimmage yards in eight consecutive games to start the season, Warren has produced just 75 yards without a touchdown over the past two games. Warren and Dowdle should continue to split backfield touches Friday against the Broncos.

4702555.headline: Coleman rushed 15 times for 26 yards and caught eight of 10 targets for 46 yards in Friday's 27-5 loss to the Steelers.
4702555.story: Coleman easily led Denver's backfield with 23 touches while Cody Shrader had seven carries and Tyler Badie had one in the latter's return from an IR stint due to a thumb injury. J.K. Dobbins will be eligible to return from a team-imposed one-game suspension in Week 13 against the Dolphins, while RJ Harvey (knee) could come off IR by then as well, but Coleman has established himself as the top option in Denver's crowded backfield. Over the past four games, Coleman has turned 67 carries and 20 catches into 393 yards from scrimmage and five touchdowns.

3121023.headline: Goedert (shoulder) had his right arm in a sling following Thursday's 39-38 victory over the Cowboys, Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reports.
3121023.story: Goedert injured his right shoulder during the first half of Thursday's game and was not cleared to return. He'll undergo further tests to determine the severity of the injury, but the veteran tight end is certainly in jeopardy of not being available for the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6. Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz and rookie second-rounder Eli Stowers would all be in line for larger roles on offense if Goedert were to miss time.

3121023.headline: Goedert (shoulder) has been ruled out of Thursday's contest at Dallas.
3121023.story: Before he jogged to the locker room and was considered questionable to return to Week 12 action, Goedert hauled in one of two targets for nine yards. With Grant Calcaterra a healthy scratch Thursday, Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz and Eli Stowers are the Eagles' healthy and available tight ends.

3121023.headline: Goedert suffered a shoulder injury during Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
3121023.story: Goedert jogged to the locker room in the first quarter and was called questionable to return by the Eagles not long afterward. For as long as Goedert remains out of the contest, Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz and Eli Stowers will handle TE duties for Philadelphia.

3121023.headline: The Eagles listed Goedert (shin) as a full participant in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
3121023.story: Philadelphia deemed Goedert a limited participant on Monday's estimated injury report, but had the team held a traditional practice Tuesday, the veteran tight end would have been able to increase his activity. Goedert thus looks on track to play Thursday, when he'll face off against a Cowboys defense that he burned for five receptions for 48 yards on seven targets back in Week 7.

4689936.headline: Bates made both of his field-goal attempts and three of his four extra-point tries during Detroit's 39-35 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
4689936.story: Bates' missed extra point came from 48 yards out due to a 15-yard taunting penalty. The 27-year-old has now converted 19 of his 21 field-goal attempts and 36 of his 37 extra-point tries across 11 games this season.

4689936.headline: Bates made one of two field-goal attempts and all four PATs in Sunday's 31-21 win over the Bucs.
4689936.story: The kicker missed a 53-yard try on the Lions' opening drive of the game but later came back to make one from 56 yards in the second quarter. Through 10 games this season, Bates is 17-for-19 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 33-for-33 on extra points. Bates led the league in PATs in the 2024 and 2025 seasons and is again on pace to kick 50-plus extra points in 2026.

4689936.headline: Bates made all five of his PATs in the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
4689936.story: Bates did not attempt a field goal in the contest. He remains 16-for-17 on field-goal attempts and moves to 29-for-29 on PATs through nine regular-season games in 2026.

4689936.headline: Bates went 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Sunday's 19-9 win over the Dolphins.
4689936.story: Bates was able to make multiple field goals for the third straight game after having done so just once over the team's first five contests this year. The kicker converted attempts from 28 and 40 yards in the first half before adding makes from 33 and 43 yards after the break. Bates has now gone 16-for-17 on field-goal tries while making all 24 of his PATs over eight games during the 2026 campaign to this point.

8439.headline: Rodgers went unclaimed on waivers and is now a free agent, Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix reports.
8439.story: Rodgers went on waivers after being cut loose by the Steelers on Thursday, and no team elected to claim him and the $8.56 million remaining on his contract. Rodgers is now able to sign with any team, but it's unclear what his next move will be.

8439.headline: The Steelers waived Rodgers on Wednesday.
8439.story: After announcing late Tuesday that Rodgers had been demoted from the starting role, the Steelers formally cut ties with him a day later following his critical comments of head coach Mike McCarthy during an interview on "The Pat McAfee Show." McGowan can be safely ruled out for the Week 12 game against the Giants, though a Week 13 bye could help the 25-year-old back avoid additional absences beyond that.

4686468.story: McGowan was injured just before halftime while returning a kickoff. He was deemed questionable to return at the beginning of the third quarter and subsequently was ruled out shortly thereafter. 4372016.story: Waddle sustained a concussion in the Broncos' last game in Week 9 at Carolina, but with the benefit of a Week 10 bye, he had enough time to gain clearance from the protocol for head injuries and miss no additional time as a result. With a 24-yard connection with QB Bo Nix on Sunday, Waddle now has recorded exactly one catch of at least that distance in four straight games. Unfortunately for Waddle's fantasy managers, his 61 receiving yards marked his second most of the campaign after a 138-yard outburst in Week 2 against the Jaguars, so he remains an underwhelming asset in most formats.

4372016.headline: Waddle (concussion) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders after practicing fully this week.
4372016.story: Waddle was limited to just 14 snaps and one catch for 22 yards before exiting the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers with a concussion. Following a well-time Week 10 bye, Waddle has progressed through the NFL's concussion protocol, ensuring that Denver's top pass catcher -- who has recorded a 30/337/2 receiving line on 52 targets through nine contests -- will be available this weekend.

4685512.headline: Price posted nine carries for 36 yards and one touchdown and gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory at Las Vegas.
4685512.story: This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

4685512.headline: Price posted nine carries for 24 yards and secured all four targets for 54 yards during Sunday's 17-3 victory versus the Cardinals.
4685512.story: Price received one more touch than Week 8's 12 but more than doubled his yards from scrimmage from 37 to 78. Having said that, backfield mate Zach Charbonnet went from nine touches last Monday against the Bears to 17 in Week 9 while pacing the Seahawks in total yards with 86. Price and Charbonnet appear poised to split the RB reps moving forward, but the former may be the change-of-pace option while the latter handles early downs.

4685512.headline: Price rushed 10 times for 29 yards and brought in two of four targets for eight yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night.
4685512.story: Making his return from a four-game stay on injured reserve due to a chest injury, Price ended up leading the Seahawks' ground attack in carries and rushing yards. Price's return coincided with the season debut of Zach Charbonnet (knee), who logged six carries in his own right in a game whose script eventually turned unfriendly to the running game. Monday may have served as a preview of what might be expected in terms of the division of labor between the two players, but more information will be gleaned during a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday that should afford both backs m

3916387.headline: The Ravens believe "there's a chance" that Jackson (thumb) could return for their Week 16 matchup with the Browns, assuming all goes well in his recovery from right thumb surgery, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.
3916387.story: Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.

3916387.headline: Jackson (thumb) is "doing well" and is expected to be out for "6-to-10 weeks," per head coach Jesse Minter.
3916387.story: Minter's statement confirmed previous reports that Jackson is both recovering from a "broken and dislocated thumb" and also that he is facing a recovery timeline of at least six weeks. It did not confirm that Jackson underwent surgery, but per Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com a procedure has been performed, and Jackson is not due back before Week 16. Jackson informed teammates earlier this month that he plans to return this season, but that will hinge on how his recovery progresses and presumably whether or not the Ravens are in playoff contention late in the campaign. Jacoby Brissett, who was rece

3916387.headline: Jackson, who is scheduled to undergo surgery on his injured right thumb, has told teammates he plans to return later this season, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
3916387.story: Jackson dislocated and fractured his right thumb on his only play of last Sunday's loss at Buffalo, and while he was placed on injured reserve Thursday, he hasn't been ruled out for the season. Considering the typical recovery for his particular injury is in the 6-to-9-week range, per Rapoport, Jackson has a chance to return before the end of the regular season, but the Ravens will need to stay in the playoff hunt. To that end, Baltimore obtained Jacoby Brissett from Arizona this week to bolster a QB room that not only lost Jackson indefinitely but also Tyler Huntley for the season due to a tu

3916387.headline: Jackson's odds to play again this season depend on his recovery from a right thumb injury, and also whether or not new QB Jacoby Brissett can keep the Ravens in the playoff picture long enough to make a return late in the season possible for Jackson, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
3916387.story: The Ravens already have cycled through three starting QBs this season, and with Tyler Huntley sidelined for the rest of the campaign due to a turf-toe injury and Jackson out indefinitely, the team agreed to a trade with the Cardinals for Brissett, which became official Friday. Brissett was serviceable until he wasn't in Arizona, finishing his 2026 season there with 1,719 yards on 63 percent passing, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight appearances, and he'll have top talents in RB Derrick Henry and WR Zay Flowers to work with in his new locale. It remains to be seen if Baltimore, whi

4360248.headline: Pitts brought in four of five targets for 50 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
4360248.story: The veteran tight end had a slow start to the day before coming on when the Falcons went especially pass-heavy in the second half. Pitts' fumble, his first of the season, came with just over four minutes remaining in the game after the contest was out of reach, and his catch total was his highest since Week 7. Pitts remains a key complementary option in an Atlanta passing attack that's scuffled of late, and he'll look to bounce back after the Falcons emerge from a Week 11 bye with a Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

4360248.headline: Pitts caught three of five targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.
4360248.story: It was another quiet performance from Pitts, who hasn't reached 25 receiving yards in any of the last three games, and he had to watch backup tight end Charlie Woerner catch Michael Penix's only TD pass of the afternoon in the first quarter. Pitts will take a 25-220-4 line on 37 targets through nine contests into a Week 10 clash with Kansas City.

4360248.headline: Week 8 winners and losers: Burrow, Higgins, Chase steal the show; Falcons falter
4360248.story: Week 8 of the 2026 fantasy football season featured huge games by three Cincinnati Bengals -- Joe Burrow, Tee Higgins and

4571557.headline: Shrader went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
4571557.story: Shrader opened Thursday's scoring with a 34-yard field goal early in the first quarter. Those ended up being the only three points scored by the Colts, as Shrader missed a 56-yarder later in the quarter, and his 62-yarder in the second quarter was blocked by Logan Hall. It was the second time this season that Shrader has missed two kicks, and the third-year kicker now is 24-for-28 on field-goal attempts (including 9-for-12 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 19-for-20 on extra-point tries through 11 regular-season games. His scoring potential figures to be lower for the rest of the season after t

4571557.headline: Shrader made his sole field-goal attempt and converted all three PATs in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
4571557.story: Shrader sole field-goal attempt was a 51-yard make in the third quarter of Sunday's contest. The kicker moves to 23-for-25 on field-goal attempts and 19-for-20 on PATs through 10 games of the 2026 regular season.

4571557.headline: Shrader went 3-for-3 on field-goal tries and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
4571557.story: Shrader entered Week 9 having made just three field goals over the team's last three games, but he got back on track Sunday. The kicker made a 47-yard attempt in the third quarter before adding makes from 59 and 50 yards in the final quarter. Shrader has now converted multiple field-goal attempts in six contests this year, and he's gone 22-for-24 on field-goal tries, including 8-for-9 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

4571557.headline: Shrader made his sole PAT in the Colts' 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
4571557.story: Shrader did not have a very active night, making the sole kick he was called upon for. He's now 14-for-15 on PATs while remaining 19-for-21 on field-goal attempts through eight regular-season games in 2026.

4685247.headline: Allen rushed 16 times for 75 yards while catching his lone target for nine yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
4685247.story: Allen's 16 carries matched his total from the previous two games combined, as he had seen a downtick in opportunities since fellow RB Breece Hall returned from a quadriceps injury. Hall led the backfield once again with 100 scrimmage yards and a touchdown on 23 touches, but Allen was a key part of the game plan as well in the run-heavy win. The Jets will face a one-win team for a second consecutive game in Week 12 at Miami, which could allow Allen to stay involved alongside Hall.

4685247.headline: Allen rushed eight times for 40 yards and caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
4685247.story: For a second consecutive game, Allen was outplayed by Breece Hall, who produced 108 scrimmage yards on 15 touches. Allen remains the more efficient runner, averaging 5.0 yards per carry to Hall's 3.4 this season, but Hall is the team's preferred option in passing situations, which have been plentiful with the 2-8 Jets frequently in catch-up mode. Perhaps a Week 11 matchup with a Chargers team that's still searching for its first win through Sunday of Week 10 will offer an opportunity to stick with the run and play to Allen's strengths.

4685247.headline: What to know to set your lineup: Cousins' Vikings return elevates Jefferson
4685247.story: Have you ever been in a relationship that was so bad, you yearned for the one who got away? Because if you did, you might just be the Minnesota Vikings. And that bad relationship might be with Carson Wentz. Just kidding. It was with Wentz. And the rift was very public, too, happening on "Monday Night Football."

4429059.headline: Marks (concussion) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
4429059.story: Marks, who was inactive Nov. 19 against the Colts, logged 'full' listings at practice Wednesday through Friday and now has gained clearance to rejoin the lineup after being sidelined for one game. His Week 11 absence coincided with the return to action of fellow RB David Montgomery, and now that both backs are available for the first time since Week 5, look for Marks to see a noticeable dip in volume while sharing touches with Montgomery, who logged 26 carries versus Indianapolis.

4429059.headline: Marks (concussion) was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
4429059.story: Marks didn't practice last week before being ruled out for this past Thursday's 26-3 win over the Colts, but with some extra recovery time since then, the running back is trending toward a return to the lineup Sunday against the Ravens. To get there, however, he'll need to fully progress through the NFL's concussion protocol in the days leading up to the Texans' Week 12 contest.

4429059.headline: Marks (concussion) was on the practice field Wednesday, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle  reports.
4429059.story: Marks, who was inactive for last Thursday's game against the Colts, was, as of Monday, "trending in the right direction," according to coach DeMeco Ryans, per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston. The running back's presence for Wednesday's session supports that notion, with Marks' official participation level in line to provide key context ahead of this Sunday's matchup against the Ravens.

4429059.headline: Head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that Marks (concussion) is "trending in the right direction," and the Texans "are hopeful to have him" for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
4429059.story: After sustaining a concussion in a Nov. 15 loss to the Browns, Marks was unable to clear the five-step protocol on a short week and ended up sitting out this past Thursday's 26-3 win over the Colts. Since then, Marks appears to have progressed on some level through the protocol, though it's not yet clear if he'll be available to practice when the Texans kick off Week 12 prep Wednesday. If Marks ends up getting the green light to play versus the Ravens, he may be part of a timeshare in the backfield or be forced to settle for No. 2 duties behind David Montgomery (groin), who returned from a fou

3128429.headline: Sutton caught one of eight targets for four yards in Friday's 27-5 loss to the Steelers.
3128429.story: Denver's entire offense struggled mightily, generating just three points while allowing Pittsburgh's defense to score two touchdowns off turnovers by Bo Nix. Sutton was right down there with Nix among Friday's worst performers in an outing reminiscent of Week 4 at San Francisco, when Sutton caught one of six targets for four yards. The 31-year-old WR has caught just one of 10 targets over the past two games, and Sutton has secured less than half of his targets (26 of 56) heading into a Week 13 home game against the Dolphins.

3128429.headline: Sutton didn't corral either of his two targets during Sunday's 38-24 victory versus the Raiders.
3128429.story: Sutton thus was blanked in the box score for the first time Week 7 of the 2024 campaign, a span of 39 games (including playoffs). Considering he's surpassed 50 receiving yards just one time in 10 appearances in 2026, he doesn't hold much sway for fantasy purposes, especially in a Broncos offense that often has sputtered this season. Sutton's next chance to turn the tide arrives Friday at Pittsburgh.

3128429.headline: Sutton caught five of nine targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
3128429.story: The five grabs and nine targets led the Broncos on the day, but Pat Bryant just edged him out for the receiving yards lead. The highlight of Sutton's solid performance was a three-yard TD from Bo Nix in the first quarter, as none of his receptions went for longer than 12 yards. Denver gets a well-timed bye in Week 10, but if Jaylen Waddle (concussion) isn't cleared to play on the other side of it, Sutton could see bigger volume in Week 11 against the Raiders. On the season, the long-time Bronco sports a 25-266-2 line on 46 targets through nine games.

3128429.headline: Sutton caught all four of his targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.
3128429.story: For the fourth straight game, Sutton failed to see more than five targets, but his four grabs and 53 yards were both season highs. It's been a rough campaign so far for the 31-year-old receiver in an inconsistent Broncos aerial attack, and Sutton will take a 20-221-1 line on 37 targets through eight games intro a Week 9 clash with the Panthers.

17372.headline: Boswell went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his lone PAT in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
17372.story: This was a battle of Pennsylvania's kickers, as Boswell and Jake Elliott combined to account for 23 of the game's 35 points. Boswell was good from 25, 40 and 52 yards. The veteran kicker has been trending downward the last two seasons, and he entered play Sunday having made just 79.2 percent of his field-goal tries this season. After his perfect showing against the Eagles, Boswell has made all of his field goals in back-to-back games for the first time all season. On the year, he's 22-for-27 on FGAs and a perfect 18-for-18 on PATs.

17372.headline: Boswell made his sole field-goal attempt and sole PAT in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
17372.story: Boswell had an uneventful night, making his 45-yard field goal in the second quarter of the contest. The kicker moves to 19-for-24 on field-goal attempts and 17-for-17 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.

17372.headline: Boswell made two of his three field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
17372.story: Boswell missed a 57-yard attempt on the Steelers' first offensive drive of the game. The kicker proceeded to nail 20-yard and 37-yard attempts en route to five straight made kicks. Boswell is now 18-for-23 on field-goal attempts and 16-for-16 on PATs through eight regular-season games in 2026.

17372.headline: Boswell made each of his three field-goal attempts and his lone extra-point try in a 16-10 victory over the Saints on Sunday in Paris.
17372.story: Boswell opened Sunday's contest with a 28-yard chip shot early in the first quarter before connecting on field goals from 47 and 39 yards in the second and third, respectively. It's the third time this season that he has made at least three field goals, and through seven regular-season games, he is 16-for-20 on field-goal attempts (including 4-for-6 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 13-for-13 on extra-point tries. The Steelers will return home for a Week 8, AFC North showdown against the Browns on Nov. 1.

4371733.headline: Gainwell rushed four times for 16 yards and brought in four of five targets for 43 yards in the Buccaneers 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
4371733.story: Gainwell held his usual complementary role on the ground behind a busy Bucky Irving, yet with the Buccaneers trailing throughout the second half, Gainwell was able to finish second in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the day for Tampa Bay. The veteran back has back-to-back 16-yard efforts on the ground, but Gainwell has a combined 7-103-0 line through the air in that same span heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.

4362081.headline: Dicker made his lone field-goal attempt and all three PATs in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
4362081.story: Dicker's field goal was drilled from 52 yards, and he's now 19-for-21 on field-goal tries and 15-for-15 on extra points through 10 games this season. In a Chargers offense struggling mightily to score points, Dicker's fantasy value has tanked this season.

4362081.headline: Dicker made all three of his field-goal tries and converted both of his extra-point attempts during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
4362081.story: Dicker's longest field goal on the day was only from 38 yards out, but his accuracy played a big part in the Chargers picking up their first win of the season. He hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, but the team's general inability to move the ball consistently keeps him from projecting as a top-tier fantasy option in most formats going into a Week 11 matchup versus the Jets.

4362081.headline: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 44-22 loss to Houston.
4362081.story: Dicker was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game and fifth time this season. The kicker did all his damage in the first half, converting field goals from 52, 33 and 43 yards before the break. Dicker has now gone 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

4362081.headline: Dicker made all three of his field-goal attempts during Sunday's 24-9 loss against the Rams. He did not kick any extra-point tries.
4362081.story: The Chargers offense put forth another poor effort in Week 8, with four of their 11 drives ending in punts and another three ending with turnovers. Dicker has mostly been efficient through his first seven games of the season, making 12 of his 14 field-goal attempts, but until the offense demonstrates it can consistently move the ball down the field, he'll be hard to trust as a fantasy option.

3116365.headline: Andrews caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to Carolina.
3116365.story: While the veteran tight end showed some instant chemistry with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett last week, Andrews saw his target volume crater in their second game together, as rookie depth TEs Josh Cuevas and Matthew Hibner saw similar usage as pass catchers. Andrews has failed to reach 25 receiving yards in five of his last six games and hasn't scored a TD in seven straight contests, making him a very risky fantasy option in Week 12 against the Texans.

3116365.headline: Andrews brought in all eight targets for 82 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday.
3116365.story: According to Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site, Andrews confirmed after Monday's game that he's been playing through a broken left hand since Week 3, but he finally appears to be back to full health. Though he didn't miss any time due to broken hand, he was listed on the injury report from Weeks 4 through 9 before avoiding the report entirely for Week 10. He proceeded to deliver a season-best performance in starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett's team debut, eclipsing his previous-best mark in receiving yardage by 33 yards. Andrews' instant chemistry with Brissett was certainly encouraging

3116365.headline: Andrews secured both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.
3116365.story: The veteran tight end actually led the Ravens in receiving yards with his modest total, as fill-in signal-caller Joe Fagnano averaged just 3.3 yards per attempt and totaled 60 passing yards overall. Andrews opened the season with back-to-back 49-yard tallies on 10 total catches, but he's been stuck at 28 receiving yards or fewer in his seven subsequent games. Andrews will hope to benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett, who should bring some stability and productivity to Baltimore's currently embattled quarterback situation.

3116365.headline: Andrews caught three of four targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills.
3116365.story: Though Lamar Jackson (ankle) made his long-awaited return to the lineup, his stay lasted just one offensive snap Sunday before he suffered a serious thumb injury. Tyler Huntley then exited the game with a toe injury in the second quarter, forcing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into emergency QB duties. No Ravens player produced even 25 receiving yards against Buffalo. Andrews has been in an extended slump and won't be a trustworthy fantasy tight end for Thursday night against the Jaguars.

3054850.headline: Kamara rushed one time for one yard and caught a one-yard touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
3054850.story: The veteran running back played just eight of 72 offensive snaps, while both CJ Donaldson and Travis Etienne played 32 each with Audric Estime a healthy inactive. Kamara has touched the ball just seven times on 24 snaps over the past two weeks, but he's turned three of those touches into short touchdowns. The Saints' three-man backfield continues to be one to try and avoid when making fantasy lineup decisions. Kamara's proverbial gas tank is nearing empty, but the Saints continue to give him high-value touches near the goal line while refusing to play him outside of the red zone.

3054850.headline: Kamra rushed two times for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added three catches for 10 yards and an additional touchdown on four targets.
3054850.story: With Travis Etienne back from his weeks-long hamstring injury that saw him miss five games while on injured reserve, the Saints deployed a three-man backfield committee against Carolina. Kamara scored a couple touchdowns, but it was a fluky performance on just five touches and 16 offensive snaps. Audric Estime logged 27 snaps and handled eight touches, while Etienne played 21 snaps and touched the ball 11 times. This is a backfield to avoid in fantasy while it the trio cancels each other out and caps each others' upside.

3054850.story:
Making tough lineup decisions each week can be the most challenging part of the fantasy football process. When you're torn between two similar players and simply don't know which to start, start the player with the superior matchup.

Ah, but exactly how does one determine the best (and worst) weekly matchups?
